decisions.reason: As a prominently launched next-generation core printer platform, it is close to the firm’s established machinery business, carries visible sunk investment, and fits the firm’s stated direction in industrial marking and traceability.

This software module extends the existing coding offer into variable-data and numbering functions, so management is likely to continue it because it supports digitalization and earlier public commitments can still be justified as needing more market adoption time.

An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces deepens the core product range for demanding applications, and a large growing German engineering firm would be inclined to persist with such a technically related product despite any early uncertainty.

Although the app is somewhat more peripheral than the hardware systems, it was given its own page and presented as the successor to an earlier app, which increases commitment and makes management likely to retain it as part of the traceability ecosystem.

Inline code verification is strategically tied to serialization, compliance and end-to-end traceability, so despite limited visibility in the archive the firm has strong reasons to continue backing it.

Because the print layout design software was shown on the home page and directly supports common operation across systems, management is likely to keep it and view any weaker results as temporary in a broader digitalization push.
